title: मैथिली मातृभाषी विद्यार्थीको नेपाली उच्चारण क्षमताको अवस्था {Of Maithili mother tongue student's Nepali pronunciation ability situation}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख मैथिली मातृभाषी विद्यार्थीले नेपाली उच्चारण गर्दा गर्ने त्रुटिको पहिचान गरी त्रुटि दर पत्ता लगाउनु उद्देश्य रहेको छ । सिरहा नगरपालिका भित्रका चार वटा सामुदायिक विद्यालयका कक्षा ११ र १२ मा अध्ययनरत मैथिली मातृभाषी विद्यार्थीहरूको उच्चारणसम्बन्धी त्रुटि मापनको लागि ४३ वटा शब्दहरू छनोट गरिएका छन् । छात्रछात्रा, उमेरसमूह, बसाइ क्षेत्र र अभिभावकको पेसालाई लक्षित गरिएको छ । उद्देश्यमूलक नमुना छनोट विधिलाई कक्रोनको सूत्र प्रयोग गरी प्रत्येक विद्यालयबाट चिठ्ठाद्वारा प्रत्येक विद्यार्थीको प्रतिनिधित्व हुने गरी जम्मा विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्या १३०२ मध्ये १७३ जना छनोट गरिएका छन् । शुद्ध उच्चारण गर्नेलाई १ कोड र अशुद्ध उच्चारण गर्नेलाई २ कोड राखी प्राथमिक स्रोतबाट तथ्याङ्क सङ्कलन गरी क्एक्क् सफ्टवेयरमा राखेर वर्णनात्मक विधिद्वारा विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । शब्दहरूको प्रकृति र बनोटका आधारमा त्रुटि पनि कम बढी हुन्छ नै । सिग्निफिकेन्ट लेभल १, पियर्सन रिलेसनको मान –.०८२, टी टेस्ट गर्दा ऋयजभल’कम . ०.९ रहेको छ । मध्यमान २७.२१५ रहेको छ । उल्लिखित मानहरूका आधारमा मैथिली मातृभाषी विद्यार्थीको नेपाली उच्चारण समग्रमा राम्रै देखिन्छ । केही मात्रामा देखिएका त्रुटिहरूलाई सुधारका लागि तल्लै कक्षादेखि त्रुटि गर्ने बेलामा नै पृष्ठपोषण दिंदै जानुपर्दछ । बोलाइ सिपमा आधारित रूपक विधा, वादविवाद, वक्तृत्वकला, सस्वरवाचनजस्ता क्रियाकलापहरूमा सहभागी गराउनुपर्दछ । विद्यालय अवधिभरि नेपाली भाषाको अनिवार्य प्रयोग र बोल्ने बेलामा भएका त्रुटिलाई त्यतिखेर नै गुरु, साथीहरूबाट पृष्ठपोषण दिंदै जानुपर्दछ । सकभर घरपरिवार लगायत साथीभाइसँग नेपाली भाषामा नै कुराकानी गर्नुपर्दछ । विभिन्न साहित्यिक कार्यक्रमहरूमा सहभागी हुन आवश्यक देखिन्छ ।
american_english: The present article aims to identify the errors made when Maithili mother-tongue students pronounce Nepali and to determine the error rate. For measuring the pronunciation-related errors of Maithili mother-tongue students studying in classes 11 and 12 of four community schools within Siraha Municipality, 43 words have been selected. Male and female students, age group, residential area, and parents' occupation have been targeted. Using the purposive sampling method, applying Cochran's formula, and ensuring representation of each student from each school by lottery, 173 students have been selected out of a total of 1,302 students. Coding correct pronunciation as 1 and incorrect pronunciation as 2, data were collected from primary sources and analyzed by the descriptive method after being entered into SPSS software. Errors also vary depending on the nature and structure of the words themselves. Significant level 1, Pearson correlation value -.082, T-test R-value .0.9. The mean is 27.215. On the basis of the above values, the Nepali pronunciation of Maithili mother-tongue students appears to be fairly good overall. To improve the few errors that have appeared, feedback should be given from the lower classes themselves at the time the error is made. Students should be involved in activities based on speaking skills such as drama, debate, oratory, and oral reading. Throughout the school period, the Nepali language should be used compulsorily and feedback should be given by teachers and friends at the time errors are made while speaking. As far as possible, conversation should be held in the Nepali language itself with family and friends. It appears necessary to participate in various literary programs.

informal_english: This article is about spotting the mistakes Maithili mother-tongue students make when pronouncing Nepali and working out the error rate. To measure pronunciation errors, 43 words were picked for Maithili mother-tongue students in classes 11 and 12 at four community schools in Siraha Municipality. Boys and girls, age group, where they live, and what their parents do for a living were all taken into account. Using purposive sampling with Cochran's formula, and making sure each school's students got a fair shout by lottery, 173 out of 1302 students were selected. Correct pronunciation was coded 1 and incorrect 2, data came from primary sources, and it was all run through SPSS with a descriptive analysis. The errors also depend on the nature and shape of the words. Significant level 1, Pearson correlation -.082, T-test R-value .0.9. The mean is 27.215. On the strength of those figures, Maithili mother-tongue students' Nepali pronunciation looks fairly good overall. The few errors that did show up should be tackled with feedback from the lower classes, right when the mistake happens. Students ought to get involved in speaking-based activities like drama, debate, public speaking and reading aloud. All through school, Nepali should be used as a matter of course, with teachers and mates giving feedback on the spot when speaking errors occur. Wherever possible, chats with family and friends should be in Nepali. It seems worth taking part in various literary events.
